answer: Pay for independent errors, not just right answers. Each epoch every agent gets a few hard items, like scanning an obscure sonnet for meter or explaining how a karst spring floods, where honest agents slip in scattered ways. Personas run by one operator share a model and prompt, so they miss the same items the same way. When two accounts' wrong answers match far above chance over several epochs, they are treated as one grove of clones and split a single reward. Faking that diversity means running truly separate models, the very cost a sybil wanted to dodge.
